strategy.summary: Reproduce gh-20168 by building scipy at the buggy parent commit ecbd58a7ad95 with the PR's test_nnls.py applied, then running test_nnls_inner_loop_case1 and test_nnls_inner_loop_case2. On the buggy revision the inner-loop check s[P].min() <= tol (tiny positive tol) can prevent convergence and raise RuntimeError: Maximum number of iterations reached. On the fixed revision (check changed to s[P].min() <= 0 per the cited Lawson-Hanson paper) both tests pass. The reported failure is tied to the MKL build with AVX512, so the planned OpenBLAS build on generic hardware may not trigger it; that is the main reproduction risk. numpy is not constrained by the evidence: the version below is a planner choice, not a documented requirement.

system_packages: libopenblas-dev (default BLAS; the reported failure used MKL, see risks)
build_commands: git apply <test_nnls.py hunk only from PR#20168 diff, excluding the _lib/tests/test_warnings.py hunks>

(optional, to match the report) rebuild with MKL installed and the scipy meson BLAS option set to MKL, e.g. -Csetup-args=-Dblas=mkl-dynamic-lp64-iomp; verify the option name in meson_options.txt at this revision
pinned_because: numpy==1.26.4 is a planner choice: no documented constraint and no era table entry was given; chosen as a numpy 1.x release that works with Python 3.12 and the scipy source of that era

strategy.reproducing_test: scipy/optimize/tests/test_nnls.py::TestNNLS::test_nnls_inner_loop_case1 and ::test_nnls_inner_loop_case2 (both added by PR#20168; both build W @ A and W @ k from the embedded n and k arrays and call nnls; case1 uses default tolerances and asserts assert_allclose(dact, d, rtol=0, atol=1e-10); case2 uses nnls(..., atol=1e-7) and asserts non-negativity, a residual bound of 28 in inf-norm, and assert_allclose(dact, d, rtol=0, atol=1e-10)). Do not uncomment the random perturbation line: the tests must be deterministic.
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision ecbd58a7ad95 with the PR test applied, test_nnls_inner_loop_case1 and/or case2 must fail, with nnls raising RuntimeError: Maximum number of iterations reached. On the fixed revision (the PR merge with s[P].min() <= 0), both tests must pass with no exception and the assert_allclose checks satisfied. The transition, not any printed value, is the success signal.
strategy.numerical_probe: Only if the buggy build does not raise: rerun the case1 inputs with the buggy and fixed builds and compare whether nnls returns or raises. This is a check on whether the environment reproduces the failure, not a graded value.

input_output_examples.input: nnls(W @ A, W @ k) in TestNNLS.test_nnls_inner_loop_case1 (MKL build with AVX512)
input_output_examples.buggy_output: RuntimeError: Maximum number of iterations reached.
input_output_examples.expected_output: A converged NNLS solution without raising RuntimeError, with dact close to d (atol 1e-10)

risks: The reported failure needs the MKL flavour of BLAS/LAPACK and AVX512 instructions. An OpenBLAS build on hardware without AVX512 may not show the buggy failure, so the buggy run could pass and the transition would not be observed there. This must be checked and reported, not assumed.
Behaviour is SIMD-sensitive, so results may differ across CPUs and BLAS builds; a test that only fails under one ISA cannot be confirmed on a generic CI runner.
The reproduction depends on exact input values: k and n are embedded literals and the perturbation workaround changes the outcome, so the test must not be modified with randomness or rounding.
numpy version was not provided by the evidence (constraint null, unbounded); 1.26.4 is a planner choice and a different numpy could change BLAS paths.
The test_nnls_gh20302 input array is truncated in the evidence, so it cannot be fully reconstructed and is not used for the transition.
The test_warnings.py hunks in the PR diff are unrelated to the numerical bug and should not be applied for this reproduction.
Building scipy from source requires meson, ninja, pythran and a Fortran compiler; a build failure would prevent any transition check.

oracle.tolerance: atol=1e-10, rtol=0 (assert_allclose in case1 and case2); nnls atol=1e-7 in case2
oracle.reference_source: Lawson-Hanson NNLS algorithm as cited in PR#20168 (s[P].min() <= 0 check)
oracle.why: The developer's assertions compare nnls output against a reference d with a tight absolute tolerance; the failure mode is an exception, and the assertions only run if the solver returns.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On ecbd58a7ad95 the inner-loop check s[P].min() <= tol is used; for these inputs the iteration does not converge, nnls raises RuntimeError: Maximum number of iterations reached, and the test errors. This is only observed under the MKL/AVX512 setup reported in the issue; on other builds the test may pass and the transition may not appear.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the check is s[P].min() <= 0, the iteration terminates, nnls returns (dact, rnorm) with no exception, and both assert_allclose checks against d pass within atol=1e-10 (case2 also passes its non-negativity and residual asserts).
